AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  NOVEMBER 1, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  5:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  CLOSED SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT
  CODE §54956.9(d)(1) City of Norwalk vs. Regional Water Quality Control Board, Case No.
  21STCP04148.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT
  CODE §54956.9(d)(1), Case No. 22STCV33737.

RECESS

REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Randy Bradley
  Apostolic Lighthouse Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Estrella Sanchez
  Gauldin Elementary School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize Clarissa Juarez, Senior Lifeguard, Caleb Goodlink, Lifeguard, and Jan
  Franco, Recreation Leader II for administering life saving measures at the Aquatics Pavilion.

  II.  City Council to recognize Johnny Figueroa, from Jovenes, for serving the Norwalk Community at the
  Social Services Center.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  State of the City Address Highlights.

  3.  Halloween Monster Mash Festival.

  4.  Bi-Weekly Review.

CONSENT CALENDAR
 Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of October
  18, 2022. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period October 2, 2022 –
  October 15, 2022, in the total amount of $1,039,685.40. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  October 11 - October 24, 2022 in the total amount of $3,890,369.03. 640

  Warrant Register

  5.  CLAIM AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Margarita Davis.
  830-04

  Report

  6.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-61 - DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS – HUMAN RESOURCES
  AND TRANSPORTATION DEPARTMENTS – Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-
  61, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE
  DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE HUMAN RESOURCES AND TRANSPORTATION
  DEPARTMENTS. 870-02

  Report

  7.  ORDINANCE NO. 22-1736 - ADDING CHAPTER 9.30 “SPEED CONTESTS OR EXHIBITIONS OF
  SPEED” TO TITLE 9 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE - Staff recommends City Council adopt
  Ordinance No. 22-1736, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK ADDING CHAPTER 9.30
  “SPEED CONTESTS OR EXHIBITIONS OF SPEED” OF TITLE 9 (“PUBLIC PEACE, MORALS AND
  WELFARE”) OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO PROHIBIT SPECTATORS AT ILLEGAL
  SPEED CONTESTS OR EXHIBITIONS OF SPEED. 735

  Report

  8.  ORDINANCE NO. 22-1737 ADDING CHAPTER 9.31 “UNLAWFUL POSSESSION OF CATALYTIC
  CONVERTERS” OF TITLE 9 (“PUBLIC PEACE, MORALS AND WELFARE”) OF THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO PROHIBIT THE UNLAWFUL POSSESSION OF CATALYTIC CONVERTERS IN
  THE CITY - Staff recommends City Council adopt Ordinance No. 22-1737, AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF NORWALK ADDING CHAPTER 9.31 “UNLAWFUL POSSESSION OF CATALYTIC
  CONVERTERS” TO TITLE 9 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE. 735

  Report

  9.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-62 - REPORTING OF THE EMPLOYER’S CONTRIBUTION FOR
  MANAGEMENT UNIT EMPLOYEES UNDER THE PUBLIC EMPLOYEES’ MEDICAL AND HOSPITAL
  CARE ACT - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-62, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK RESCINDING RESOLUTION NO. 21-57 AND FIXING
  THE EMPLOYER CONTRIBUTION AT AN EQUAL AMOUNT FOR EMPLOYEES AND ANNUITANTS
  UNDER THE PUBLIC EMPLOYEES’ MEDICAL AND HOSPITAL CARE ACT FOR MANAGEMENT
  EMPLOYEES. 135-01-03

  Report

  10. AUTHORIZE FINAL PAYMENT TO CASSO & SPARKS, LLC FOR LEGAL SERVICES RELATED TO
   THE CITY’S WASTE DISCHARGE REQUIREMENTS AND NATIONAL POLLUTANT DISCHARGE
  ELIMINATION SYSTEM PERMIT FOR MUNICIPAL SEPARATE STORM SEWER SYSTEM
  DISCHARGES - Staff recommends City Council approve final payment to Casso and Sparks, LLC, for
  Legal Services Related to Waste Discharge Requirements and National Pollutant Discharge
  Elimination System Permit for Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System discharges, in an amount not-
  to-exceed $44,314.80; and authorize the City Manager to execute any final close out agreement with
  Casso and Sparks, LLC in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1040-04

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  11. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200 ORDINANCE

  Report

ORDINANCE

  12. ORDINANCE NO. 22-1738 - 2022 CALIFORNIA BUILDING, RESIDENTIAL, FIRE, PLUMBING,
  ELECTRICAL, MECHANICAL, EXISTING BUILDING, AND GREEN BUILDING STANDARD CODES
  AND RELATED MODEL CODES - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  introduce for first reading by title only, Ordinance No. 22-1738, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK ADOPTING BY REFERENCE THE 2022 EDITIONS OF THE CALIFORNIA
  BUILDING, RESIDENTIAL, FIRE, PLUMBING, ELECTRICAL, MECHANICAL, EXISTING
  BUILDING, AND GREEN BUILDING STANDARDS CODES AND RELATED MODEL CODES,
  WITH APPENDICES AND AMENDMENTS THERETO; AND AMENDING THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE, and schedule for adoption; and

  b.  set a public hearing date for November 15, 2022. 305-01

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated October 27, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
